items.title: 52263_Sonny Greer oral history interview
items.q: A man named Beckley owned it. I played up there.

ctx.x: When you were coming up, like you were living in Washington, how did the Negro musicians look at -- how did they see the music scene. I mean, did they feel like they were getting the proper breaks, or did they feel --

Oh, they had their little -- it wasn't that rough, you know, cause there was always some affairs going on, colored affairs, and they had that little circle, they had cabarets down there for colored, had theatre, the Howard Theatre was beautiful, beautiful theatre, real pretty. Club around the corner, called the Dreamland, upstairs. A man named Beckley owned it. I played up there. Played up there. I doubled up there (unintelligible) played with Claude up

there, Claude Hopkins and a fellow named Eddie W____, and all the way (unintelligible) I didn't miss nothing, no kidding and happy,man I was very happy because everything was real fine, real fine, man.
